key_patterns.liberal_pattern: Ministers funnel contracts to friends and family. Ethics commissioner finds violations. Zero penalty. Government hides documents and is found in contempt. Party expels whistleblowers, protects wrongdoers. $400M SDTC slush fund with 186 conflicts is the crown jewel.

key_patterns.structural_problem: Ethics commissioner has NO enforcement power. No fines, no criminal referral, no removal. Findings are published and ignored. This is the core argument for P1 (criminal breach of trust) and structural reform. NEW: Champagne-Alto conflict (April 2026) proves the screening system is still broken — ministers can have partners at companies receiving $100M+ from their own budgets without it appearing in ethics filings.
key_patterns.lobbying_context: Record 6,223 active lobbying registrations (November 2024). October 2024 set all-time record with 4,509 communication reports. New 8-hour threshold (January 2026) expected to trigger massive surge in registrations. 8,884 individual lobbyists registered in 2024-25.
key_patterns.45th_parliament_notes: Carney cabinet has 9 first-time MPs in ministerial roles — untested and vulnerable to ethics exposure. Evan Solomon (former CBC broadcaster) is Minister of AI. Chrystia Freeland resigned her seat Jan 2026 to advise Ukraine government (see freeland_browder_dossier.json). Guilbeault resigned from cabinet over Alberta energy deal — internal Liberal rift. The freshness of this cabinet means new ethics violations will emerge as inexperienced ministers navigate conflict of interest rules they've never dealt with.
key_patterns.foreign_interference: NSICOP says MPs from multiple parties are 'witting' agents of China/India. Names are classified. RCMP won't investigate. Poilievre won't look at the evidence. Trudeau says he saw CPC names. This creates maximum mutual suspicion — perfect for the campaign's strategy of turning parties against each other.
